briefing: The window was quiet on model releases but notable on policy and infrastructure financing. Trump announced a new federal 'Super Intelligence Force' task force to coordinate AI policy, led by DNI Jay Clayton, days after tech executives signed a non-binding White House safety accord. On the infrastructure side, Nvidia-backed neocloud Firmus moved to price a $5.5 billion Australian IPO at a $30.6 billion valuation (roughly tripling its two-month-old private valuation), Schneider Electric agreed to buy PTC for $22.6 billion to build out AI-linked industrial software, and the US government advanced a $4.2 billion loan to Vistra to uprate nuclear capacity feeding AI data centers. A sharp, short-lived selloff and rebound in Cerebras shares over a single-customer (OpenAI) concentration scare underscored how exposed parts of the AI supply chain remain to single contracts.

roi_analysis.verdict: Capital keeps flowing into AI infrastructure, financing structures, and power at a record pace, while policy and customer-concentration risks highlighted this run show the trade still rests on assumptions that haven't been tested by a downturn.
supporting_points: Nvidia-backed neocloud Firmus is pricing a $5.5 billion IPO at a $30.6 billion valuation, nearly three times its $10.5 billion valuation from a private round just two months earlier, with investor demand reportedly exceeding the offer size (Bloomberg/TechStartups).

Schneider Electric agreed to pay $22.6 billion for PTC, its largest-ever acquisition, explicitly to build 'the industry's most complete software and AI powerhouse' by linking engineering data with its energy and industrial software (Bloomberg).

The US government is advancing a $4.2 billion loan to Vistra to uprate three nuclear plants supplying the PJM grid, a concrete sign that policymakers are committing public capital to solve the power bottleneck AI data centers face (Reuters/CNBC; Construction Review).
counter_points: Cerebras shares swung roughly 20% down and then up within days on nothing more than a rumor and a reassurance tweet about its single largest customer, OpenAI, illustrating how thin and concentrated the revenue base is for AI hardware challengers (Seeking Alpha/Yahoo Finance).

Schneider Electric's own stock fell nearly 10% (wiping out about €15 billion in market value) on the PTC deal announcement, with Jefferies flagging 'AI disruption fears' still weighing on software valuations even as the acquirer pays a steep 42% premium (Reuters).

Trump's new 'Super Intelligence Force' institutionalizes a voluntary, enforcement-light approach to AI oversight just as the FTC, state AGs, and departing safety staff raise fresh concerns, leaving the governance gap flagged in prior runs unresolved (CBS News/TechCrunch).

by_layer.infrastructure: Financing innovation keeps accelerating (Firmus IPO, federal nuclear loans, industrial-software M&A), but each deal also surfaces new stress points—richly priced follow-on rounds, acquirer share price hits, and customer-concentration risk for hardware vendors.
by_layer.labs: No new lab-level revenue or profitability disclosures this run; prior run's evidence of Anthropic's revenue lead and first positive adjusted operating income still stands as the strongest lab-level ROI signal.
by_layer.enterprise: This run's items are almost entirely supply-side (chips, power, industrial software); no new enterprise P&L evidence arrived to narrow the adoption-to-ROI gap flagged previously.

roi_analysis.what_changed: New this run: a concrete federal capital commitment to nuclear power for AI data centers and a record-setting neocloud IPO valuation jump, alongside visible market skittishness (Cerebras whiplash, Schneider's selloff) that illustrates how fragile sentiment remains; stance holds at mixed.

items.headline: Trump launches 'Super Intelligence Force' AI policy task force
items.summary: President Trump announced a new federal task force, the Super Intelligence Force, led by DNI Jay Clayton with FTC Chair Andrew Ferguson, Pentagon CTO Emil Michael, and OPM Director Scott Kupor as vice chairs, tasked with a 120-day report on AI risks and opportunities.
items.why_it_matters: It formalizes the administration's voluntary, light-touch approach to AI oversight just as the FTC probes OpenAI and Anthropic, shaping the regulatory risk backdrop for AI investment.

items.headline: Nvidia-backed Firmus targets $5.5B IPO at $30.6B valuation
items.summary: Australian AI infrastructure operator Firmus Grid is pricing a $5.5 billion IPO (including greenshoe) at about $30.6 billion, nearly triple the $10.5 billion valuation from its August private round, with Nvidia and Blackstone positioned to increase stakes.
items.why_it_matters: A near-tripling of a neocloud's valuation in two months, with investor demand exceeding the offer size, is a concrete funding-flow data point for gauging how hot AI infrastructure investment remains.
items.confidence_note: Based on Bloomberg sourcing citing people familiar with the matter; final terms were still being set at time of reporting.

items.headline: Schneider Electric to buy PTC for $22.6B to expand AI software
items.summary: Schneider Electric agreed to an all-cash $22.6 billion acquisition of industrial software maker PTC, its largest deal ever, aiming to link PTC's product-design data with Schneider's energy and operations software to support industrial AI agents.
items.why_it_matters: A sized capital flow into AI-linked industrial software shows capex spreading beyond chips and data centers, though Schneider's own stock fell nearly 10% on investor concern about the price paid.

items.headline: US advances $4.2B loan to Vistra for nuclear uprates to feed AI demand
items.summary: The Department of Energy is finalizing a roughly $4.2 billion loan guarantee for Vistra to uprate three nuclear plants serving the PJM grid, with Energy Secretary Chris Wright announcing the financing Monday at Vistra's Perry plant in Ohio.
items.why_it_matters: A direct federal capital commitment to add nuclear power capacity shows the government stepping in to solve the electricity bottleneck that increasingly constrains AI data center buildout.
items.confidence_note: DOE describes the package as a proposed loan guarantee under evaluation rather than a finalized, closed loan.

items.headline: Cerebras stock whipsaws on OpenAI customer-concentration scare
items.summary: Cerebras shares fell nearly 20% last week on reports OpenAI chose Nvidia GPUs over Cerebras chips for its new 'Ultrafast' inference tier, then rebounded over 6% after CEO Sam Altman called Cerebras a 'close partner' with 'deep engagement.'
items.why_it_matters: The swing shows how exposed AI hardware challengers remain to single-customer concentration risk, a vulnerability for the infrastructure layer of the AI trade.
